name: Linear Algebra
description: Matrix algebra, Gaussian elimination, determinants, vector spaces and linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, orthogonality. Essential foundation for DSC 40A, 120, 123A, 140A/B. Prerequisites: Math placement required.

name: Calculus and Analytic Geometry for Science and Engineering
description: Vector geometry, vector functions and their derivatives, partial differentiation, optimization, multiple integrals, and vector calculus. Required prerequisite for DSC 40A. Prerequisites: MATH 20B.

name: Introduction to Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, discrete and continuous distributions, expectation, variance, joint distributions, conditional probability, law of large numbers, central limit theorem. Required or recommended for DSC 140A, 140B, 148, 155. Prerequisites: MATH 20C.

name: Exploratory Data Analysis and Inference
description: Data analysis, statistical inference, and regression using real datasets. Recommended completion before DSC 180A. Bridges theory and practice. Prerequisites: MATH 18 and MATH 180A.

name: Principles of Data Science
description: First course in data science. Introduces data exploration, statistical inference, and prediction using Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib). Students work with real-world datasets through homework and projects. No prerequisites — open to all students.

name: Programming and Basic Data Structures for Data Science
description: Expands programming skills from DSC 10: recursion, higher-order functions, object-oriented programming, interpreters, and basic data structures (arrays, lists, linked lists). Taught in Python. Prerequisites: DSC 10. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Data Structures and Algorithms for Data Science
description: Advanced programming in Java: encapsulation, abstract data types, interfaces, algorithm complexity, stacks, queues, priority queues, heaps, linked lists, binary search trees, and hash tables. Several large programming projects. Prerequisites: DSC 20. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Data Science I
description: Mathematical theory underlying machine learning: empirical risk minimization, optimization, regression, classification, and discrete probability. Students practice rigorous mathematical reasoning and justification. Prerequisites: DSC 10, MATH 20C (or 31BH), and MATH 18 (or 20F/31AH). Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Data Science II
description: Algorithms and discrete mathematics for data science: runtime analysis, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, and combinatorics. Bridges lower- and upper-division DSC courses. Prerequisites: DSC 30 and DSC 40A. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: The Practice and Application of Data Science
description: Hands-on data science with real-world datasets: exploratory data analysis, data cleaning, feature engineering, and predictive modeling using pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn. Emphasizes the full data science lifecycle and best practices. Prerequisites: DSC 10. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Introduction to Data Management
description: Principles of relational database management: entity-relationship modeling, relational algebra, SQL (queries, joins, aggregation, subqueries), database design and normalization, transactions, and an introduction to NoSQL systems. Hands-on SQL projects with real databases. Prerequisites: DSC 40B and DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Systems for Scalable Analytics
description: Computing infrastructure for large-scale data analytics: memory hierarchy, distributed systems, MapReduce/Hadoop, Apache Spark, and deployment at scale. Students learn how dataflow operations are used for data preparation, cleaning, and feature engineering at scale. Prerequisites: DSC 100. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Beyond Relational Data Management
description: NoSQL data formats, data models, and high-level query languages for modern analytics. Topics include hierarchical databases, graph database systems (e.g., Neo4j), array databases, comparison of expressive power of data models, and parallel programming abstractions. Prerequisites: DSC 100. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Introduction to Data Visualization
description: Principles, techniques, and algorithms for creating effective data visualizations. Draws from computer graphics, HCI, cognitive psychology, and statistical graphics. Students design interactive visualization systems using D3.js or web-based tools and evaluate their effectiveness through user studies. Prerequisites: DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Signal Processing for Data Analysis
description: Classical and modern signal processing for data science: sampling theory, Fourier analysis, lossy transformations and compression, time/spatial filters, wavelets, and random Fourier features. Applies to time series, streaming signals, and image data. Prerequisites: (MATH 18 or 31AH), (MATH 20C or 31BH), and DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science I
description: Introduction to convex optimization: convex sets, convex functions, geometry of hyperplanes, support functions. Linear and quadratic programming, optimality conditions, duality, and primal/dual forms of linear support vector machines. Active-set and interior-point methods. Prerequisites: MATH 20C and MATH 18. Cannot receive credit for both DSC 123A and MATH 173A.

name: Optimization Methods for Data Science II
description: Unconstrained optimization: linear and randomized least squares, steepest descent, line-search methods, conjugate gradient, stochastic gradient methods, and nonlinear least squares. Convex constrained optimization: Lagrangian relaxation, method of multipliers, alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Prerequisites: DSC 123A or MATH 173A.

name: Probabilistic Modeling and Machine Learning
description: Probabilistic models for knowledge representation and decision-making: Bayesian networks, Markov models, temporal models, hidden Markov models, and online learning. Applications to NLP, adversarial learning, computational biology, and robotics. MATH 181A strongly recommended. Prerequisites: DSC 80 and a probability course. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Representation Learning
description: Machine learning techniques for learning representations from data: clustering, dimensionality reduction, manifold learning, PCA, spectral embeddings, multilayer perceptrons, autoencoders, convolutional networks (CNNs), recurrent networks (RNNs), and deep learning foundations. Prerequisites: DSC 80 and a probability course. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Introduction to Data Mining
description: Current methods for analyzing and mining real-world data: frequent pattern mining, association rules, classification, regression, clustering, and representation learning. Requires comfort with programming, basic optimization, and linear algebra. Prerequisites: DSC 40B, DSC 80, and a probability course. Cannot receive credit for both DSC 148 and CSE 158.

name: Hidden Data in Random Matrices
description: Rigorous treatment of PCA and random matrix theory: singular value decomposition, maximum likelihood estimation, least squares, Wigner's semicircle law, Marchenko-Pastur laws, universality of eigenvalue statistics, the BBP phase transition, and applications to community detection and stochastic block models. Prerequisites: MATH 180A and MATH 18. Cannot receive credit for both DSC 155 and MATH 182.

name: Data Science and the Arts
description: Explores the intersection of data science and contemporary arts: authorship, representation, visualization, and data provenance. Students examine problems from both artist-researcher and data scientist perspectives, working with cultural datasets. Not a pure CS or arts course — it bridges both. Prerequisites: DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Text as Data
description: Statistical and computational methods for using text as a data source in the social sciences. Topics include tokenization, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, text classification, and word embeddings. Hands-on projects with real text data. Prerequisites: DSC 80 or equivalent programming and stats background.

name: Fairness and Algorithmic Decision-Making
description: Examines the broader social context of data science: how bias and fairness issues arise in technical work, legal and ethical frameworks, auditing algorithms for discrimination, and proposing solutions. Combines data analysis with policy critique. Light workload compared to technical DSC courses. Prerequisites: DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Spatial Data Science and Applications
description: Concepts and methods for spatial data: geographic information systems (GIS), spatial big data management, geostatistics, and spatial reasoning. Applications where location, shape, and arrangement of objects are important. Introduces students to tools like GeoPandas and QGIS. Prerequisites: DSC 80. Restricted to DS25 majors.

name: Data Science Project I
description: First half of the year-long capstone sequence. Students investigate a faculty-proposed research topic spanning the full data science lifecycle: assessing the problem, learning domain knowledge, collecting/cleaning data, creating a model, and addressing ethical issues. Deliverable: research summary and project proposal. Prerequisites: DSC 102, MATH 189, and a qualifying elective. Restricted to DS25 seniors.

name: Data Science Project II
description: Second half of the capstone sequence. Students implement the project designed in DSC 180A, applying best practices for evaluation, reproducibility, and communication. Culminates in a public poster session and written report. Must enroll in the section tied to your DSC 180A section. Prerequisites: DSC 180A.

name: Topics in Data Science
description: Special topics course that changes each quarter based on faculty interest — past offerings have covered LLMs, causal inference, and time series analysis. May be taken up to four times when the topic varies. Department and instructor approval required. Restricted to upper-division students.

name: Seminar in Data Science
description: Seminar course on current topics in data science: invited speakers from academia and industry, discussions on emerging research. Topic varies by quarter. Light workload — primarily attendance and short written responses. May be taken three times. Prerequisites: upper-division standing.

name: Data Science Internship
description: Earn academic credit for an internship by connecting it to a faculty-supervised research project. Students must secure their internship independently before enrolling. The research topic should promote the principles and techniques involved in the internship work. Prerequisites: upper-division standing, instructor and department approval.

name: Directed Group Study in Data Science
description: Reading and discussion-based group study on a data science topic under faculty supervision. Small cohort format. May be taken twice for credit. Requires department stamp and Special Studies application. Prerequisites: upper-division standing and instructor approval.

name: Independent Study for Data Science Undergraduates
description: Individual research on a topic related to data science by special arrangement with a faculty member. Ideal for students exploring graduate school or deepening expertise in a research area. Requires a research proposal and regular faculty meetings. Prerequisites: upper-division standing and instructor approval.
